title: Variables

content.title: Variables store information
content.summary: A variable is like a labelled box that holds a value.
content.body:
Think of a variable like a labelled box.

You write a name on the outside, and put a value inside.

When Python sees the label later, it opens the box and uses what's inside.

In programming, we call this a variable — a named place in memory that stores a value.

content.title: Creating a variable
content.summary: Use = to put a value in the box.
content.body: In Python, `=` means "put this value in the box."
content.note:
This creates a box called `name`, puts `"Maya"` inside, then prints whatever is in the box.

We call this assigning a value — you're assigning `"Maya"` to the variable `name`.

content.title: Variables can hold different kinds of things
content.summary: Variables can store text or numbers.
content.body: Different boxes can hold different things. Text in quotes is one kind; numbers without quotes are another.
content.codeBlock:
pet = "cat"   # text in quotes — a string
age = 12       # a number
content.note:
Later you'll mix these to build things like:
"Hi, I'm Maya and I'm 12 years old." — all pulled from variables automatically.

content.title: Which one creates a variable correctly?
content.summary: Spot the right way to store text in a variable.
content.body: You want to store the word `pizza` in a variable called `food`. Which line does that?

puzzle.explanation: The variable name goes on the left, the value on the right. Text always needs quotes — without them, Python looks for a variable called `pizza` and doesn't find one.

steps.instruction: Step 1: Run the program. Then change the value inside the `name` variable to your own name and run it again.
Step 2: Create a variable called `age`. Store a number in it and print it.
Step 3: Create another variable called `food`. Store a food you like in it and print it.
Step 4: Change `name` to a different name and `age` to a different number. Run it. What changed in the output?

bonusSteps.instruction: Bonus: Build a mini profile. Create variables for a character's name, age, favorite food, and pet. Print each one on its own line.

progressiveHints:
# Variables store information under a name
name = "Taylor"
print(name)

# Create another variable and print it
name = "Taylor"
pet = "dragon"

print(name)
print(pet)

name = "Taylor"
pet = "dragon"
age = 12
food = "pizza"

print(name)
print(pet)
print(age)
print(food)

# Try changing the values and running the program again
name = "Morgan"
pet = "cat"
age = 10
food = "tacos"

print(name)
print(pet)
print(age)
print(food)
